subject: Post-call: context length & token mix — follow-up and next steps
content:
From: karthik.iyer@redwood.com
To: Alicia Gomez <alicia@brightlogistics.com>
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.com, priyom.das@redwood.com
Date: 2028-07-12T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Post-call: context length & token mix — follow-up and next steps

Alicia, thanks again for taking time this morning — quick recap and a few follow-ups so we can lock in pricing/fit before the technical deep dive.

Call highlights (my notes):
- Use cases: dynamic route planning (short prompts, short completions), multi-day shipment summarization (longer context + multi-paragraph completions), and SLA incident summarization (occasionally very long history).
- Integration mode: API-first, hybrid edge cache for latency-critical edges.
- Security/regulatory: need SOC2 + data residency conversation.

As discussed, two things we need to qualify pricing: token mix (avg prompt vs completion) and the distribution of requests across 8k/32k/128k contexts. If you can share ballpark numbers, we can produce a pricing model targeted at your target $/1M tokens. Specifically: 
1) Avg prompt tokens per request (example: 80–200)
2) Avg completion tokens per request (example: 200–800)
3) Percent of requests that require: <=8k, >8k and <=32k, >32k and up to 128k
4) Monthly request volume or total tokens/month (prompts + completions)
5) Target price per 1M tokens (if you have an internal target range) and monthly budget band ($/month)
6) Any hard latency SLOs (p95 / p99) or batch tolerance (can you accept 100–300ms added by batching?)

Attached is a very small template I use to map these inputs to SKU-level pricing and cost buckets: Bright_8k32k_profile_v1.xlsx. If you can fill columns 1–5 with estimates, we’ll run a short model and return: (a) expected $/1M under hosted API with our default batching, (b) delta for Dedicated (reserved) capacity with 8-bit quantization, (c) recommendations to reduce unit cost (KV caching, prefix caching strategies, prompt trimming).

Proposed next step: once we have those numbers, schedule a 60-minute technical deep dive with our runtime lead (Marissa) to validate integration constraints and run a short live throughput test. Are you available Tuesday or Wednesday morning next week (PST)?

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
karthik.iyer@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0104

---

On 2028-07-12T11:03:00-07:00 Alicia Gomez <alicia@brightlogistics.com> wrote:
> Thanks Karthik — great summary. I filled the quick numbers below so you can kick off the model: 
> 
> - Avg prompt tokens: 120
> - Avg completion tokens: 520
> - Request distribution by context length: ~70% <=8k, ~28% 8k-32k, ~2% 32k-128k (the 2% are our incident summary flows that pull 90–120k characters of history)
> - Monthly volume: ~2.5M API calls/month — ballpark split 40% short (notifications), 55% medium (summaries), 5% long (incident recon)
> - Estimated tokens/month: prompts ~300M tokens, completions ~1.3B tokens (total ~1.6B tokens/month)
> - Target unit economics: we’re looking to hit ~$6–8 / 1M tokens (in-hosted preferred); monthly budget target roughly $20k–$30k to start, with potential to double in 6–9 months if latency and quality hold.
> - Latency: p95 target ~400ms for short flows; for long-context batches we can tolerate p95 up to ~2s. Batch tolerance: we prefer sub-200ms added latency for short notification flows.
> 
> Happy to send a sanitized sample of a long incident payload if that helps profiling. SOC2 is a must; we’ll also need an export of your recent pen-test summary.
> 
> Cheers,
> Alicia
> Head of Platform Integrations | Bright Logistics
> alicia@brightlogistics.com

---

From: karthik.iyer@redwood.com
To: Alicia Gomez <alicia@brightlogistics.com>
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.com, priyom.das@redwood.com
Date: 2028-07-12T12:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: context length & token mix — follow-up and next steps

Alicia — this is perfect, thanks for the quick numbers. A few clarifying points and what we’ll supply back: 

Clarifications from your numbers:
- When you say avg completion = 520 tokens, is that median or mean? If you have a 90th percentile number for completion length (particularly for the 5% long flows) that helps with model tail-costs.
- The monthly tokens you gave (~1.6B) map well to two pricing paths: hosted API vs Dedicated. Hosted will likely be a bit higher $/1M but zero infra ops; Dedicated committed capacity + quantization (int8 or 4-bit FP-selective) can push unit costs down ~20–35% depending on burst profile.

What we’ll return by EOD tomorrow once we run the quick model: 
- A pricing band for hosted API ($/1M) with expected monthly invoice at current mix
- A Dedicated reserved-capacity quote (monthly commit) with expected unit $/1M and break-even point
- Specific ops levers to hit your $6–8 / 1M target (cache hit rate assumptions, batching window for short flows, quantization tradeoffs)

Two immediate recommendations that often unlock large delta on unit cost:
1) Prefix and KV caching for shipment histories — with even a 20% cache hit on completions you can cut completion token spend significantly.
2) Trim deterministic metadata out of prompts and pass as structured fields where possible (reduces avg prompt by ~10–20% depending on template).

Marissa — can you take the lead on scheduling the deep dive and draft a preliminary Dedicated vs Hosted cost comparison so we can share with Bright? Priyom — I’ll loop you in on the technical assumptions for quantization.

Thanks — I’ll attach the initial model after Marissa confirms the time.

Karthik

---

From: marissa.cole@redwood.com
To: Alicia Gomez <alicia@brightlogistics.com>, karthik.iyer@redwood.com
Date: 2028-07-13T15:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: context length & token mix — follow-up and next steps

Alicia / Karthik — looping in our runtime solutions lead and proposing two slots for the 60-min technical deep dive: Tuesday 2028-07-19 09:30–10:30 PST or Wednesday 2028-07-20 10:00–11:00 PST. Please confirm which works.

I attached a more detailed pricing workbook (prod_pricing_model_v3.xlsx) that includes: hosted API baseline, estimated unit cost per 1M tokens at current mix, Dedicated reserved SKU math, and a simple break-even chart. Also attached a short security snapshot (security-snapshot.pdf) that contains SOC2 status and redaction guidelines — we can follow up with the pen-test artifact under an NDA.

Notes from the model (high level):
- With the mix Alicia provided, hosted API baseline estimate: ~$9.2 / 1M tokens (this includes default batching and typical cache assumptions).
- Dedicated committed capacity with 4-bit mixed quantization estimate: ~$6.4 / 1M tokens (assumes 70% short flow hit with 150ms batching slack and 20% KV cache hit on completions).
- Break-even (hosted vs dedicated) estimated at ~3.5–4.0M API calls/month given your completion heavy profile.

Action items:
- Alicia: confirm slot and share the sanitized long-incident payload if possible (we’ll use it for a tailored token/speed run).
- Alicia: if you have an internal target for p99 (you mentioned p95 targets), share that so we can validate tail latency under batch strategies.
- Karthik / Priyom: prepare a short canary plan (minimal test, metrics to watch, rollback triggers).

Thanks — looking forward to the deep dive.

– Marissa Cole
Solutions Lead, Runtime | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com

Attachments: prod_pricing_model_v3.xlsx, security-snapshot.pdf
